row.task_instruction: Optimize ReaxFF force field parameters using a machine learning-guided evolutionary algorithm approach. The program should iteratively train a Random Forest regression model on parameter-score pairs and use differential evolution to explore the parameter space for improved force field performance. Start with an initial population of parameter sets, evaluate their performance scores, and then alternate between training the ML model on accumulated data and using it to guide the evolutionary search for better parameters. Save the optimized parameter history to "pred_results/ffield.csv" in CSV format with columns for each parameter name plus a score column, log the detailed optimization progress to "pred_results/evolution.log", and output the final optimization results including iteration count, final score, and convergence status to "pred_results/pred_train.json" in JSON format.

row.task_instruction: Generate comprehensive protein sequence features for structure prediction by processing a protein FASTA file and extracting multiple sequence alignment (MSA) derived features, evolutionary information, and statistical profiles. Use the input FASTA file containing the target protein sequence, along with any available auxiliary files including HMM profiles (.hhm), multiple sequence alignments (.aln or .fas), and pseudolikelihood matrices (.mat) from the same directory. The program should compute various feature representations including one-hot encoded amino acid sequences, HHblits profiles, reweighted profiles based on sequence similarity, mutual information matrices from direct coupling analysis, gap statistics, and pseudolikelihood features when available. Save the extracted features as a NumPy array containing all computed feature matrices and metadata to 'pred_results/pred_feature.npy' in pickle format, which will serve as input for downstream protein structure prediction algorithms.

Calculate molecular potential energy fluctuations for chemical bonds using van der Waals and Morse potential models. The program should compute upper and lower bounds for bond energies, van der Waals interactions, and bond orders by applying specified fluctuation percentages to the base potential energy calculations. Use the force field parameters from "benchmark/datasets/I-ReaxFF/test/ffield.json" if available, or generate sample parameters for common bond types (C-C, H-H, O-O) including gamma values, van der Waals depths, equilibrium distances, and damping factors. For bonds where CSV data files exist (following the pattern "fluct_[bond].csv" and "bo_fluct_[bond].csv"), read the distance-energy relationships from these files; otherwise generate sample data using exponential and power-law functions. Apply Morse potential calculations with harmonic corrections and van der Waals contributions, computing energy fluctuations at multiple distance points along each bond. Save the results as four JSON files in the "pred_results/" directory: "pred_fluctuation_energy.json" containing bond energy and van der Waals fluctuation bounds, "pred_fluctuation_bo.json" with bond order fluctuation data, "pred_fluctuation_morse.json" with Morse potential bounds, and "pred_fluctuation_summary.csv" as a tabular summary of the first few data points for each bond type.

Process educational sequence data using the DKT-Forget model dataset loader to analyze student learning patterns with forgetting mechanisms. Load student interaction sequences from "benchmark/datasets/pykt-toolkit/data/train_valid_sequences.csv" (or alternative paths "benchmark/datasets/pykt-toolkit/data/assist2017_sample.csv" or "train_valid_sequences.csv"), which should contain columns for concepts, questions, responses, timestamps, selectmasks, and fold information. The system will compute temporal features including repeated gaps (time intervals between repeated skill practice), sequence gaps (time intervals between consecutive interactions), and past exercise counts, applying logarithmic transformations to capture forgetting effects. Generate two output files: "pred_results/pred_dkt_forget_dataloader.json" containing the processed dataset statistics, sample data points, and tensor shapes for regular evaluation mode, and "pred_results/pred_dkt_forget_dataloader_qtest.json" for question-level evaluation mode if the required qtest columns are available in the input data.

Load and preprocess educational interaction data from "benchmark/datasets/pykt-toolkit/data/train_valid_sequences.csv" for knowledge tracing analysis. The dataset should contain student learning sequences with questions, knowledge concepts, responses, and selection masks across different folds. Process the sequential data by converting concept and question sequences into tensor format, applying appropriate padding, and creating shifted sequences for temporal modeling. Generate dataset statistics including total samples, tensor shapes, and sample sequence information, then save the processed results to "pred_results/pred_que_data_loader_promptkt.json" in JSON format with dataset statistics, sample results, and processing information.

row.task_instruction: Load neurophysiological data from NWB (Neurodata Without Borders) files using the BaseLoader class to extract behavioral tracking data, experimental epochs, and time support information from neuroscience datasets. The program should search through available test datasets in the benchmark/datasets/pynapple/tests/nwbfilestest directory structure, attempt to load data from valid NWB files, and extract key experimental metadata including animal position tracking data (such as spatial coordinates and compass direction), experimental epoch labels with their corresponding time intervals, and overall time support boundaries. Save the extracted metadata and loading results to "pred_results/pred_loader.json" in JSON format, including information about successfully loaded data types, epoch details with start/end times, position data dimensions and column names, and any loading errors encountered during the process.
